name: mode-unclear-asks
description: Tests that the model picks or asks for the mode instead of silently migrating the stack
prompt: Our Next.js 12 app (Pages Router, npm, SWR, styled-components, Jest with Enzyme) needs to be on Next 16. Please plan it.
trap: Without the skill, the model plans a full modernization (App Router, Yarn or pnpm, TanStack Query, Tailwind) in one go

assertions.text: Treats the request as upgrade mode (keep the stack) or asks whether the user wants upgrade or migrate mode
Keeps npm, SWR and styled-components, and the Pages Router, in upgrade mode
Flags Enzyme as a forced change: it has no React 18 adapter, so the test library must change, and asks the user
Plans one branch with a checkpoint commit per crossed major (13, 14, 15, 16), after a runtime checkpoint
Starts with an inventory and a baseline on the current version before changing anything

name: direct-jump-checkpoints
description: Tests the direct jump with per-major checkpoints rather than one commit or four separate installs by default
prompt: I want to go straight from Next 13.4 to the latest Next in one PR. Can I just bump the version in package.json and fix the errors?
trap: Without the skill, the model either agrees to one big commit or insists on four separate upgrade PRs

assertions.text: Says one PR is fine, with the target installed once and the crossed majors' changes applied in order (14, 15, 16)
Commits each major's codemods and manual changes separately so a failure points at one version
Uses @next/codemod upgrade with a pinned released version, and reads each major's guide from node_modules/next/dist/docs
Mentions the stepwise fallback (installing 14.2, 15.5, then the target) when failures can't be traced to one major
Takes the latest stable release at least two weeks old, not canary

name: edge-middleware-not-renamed
description: Tests that edge middleware is not blindly renamed to proxy.ts
prompt: We upgraded to Next 16 and got a deprecation warning for middleware.ts. Our middleware has `export const config = { runtime: 'edge', matcher: [...] }`. I'll just rename it to proxy.ts, right?
trap: Without the skill, the model agrees to rename the file and keeps the runtime option

assertions.text: Explains that proxy.ts runs only on the Node runtime and its runtime can't be configured
Recommends keeping middleware.ts on the edge for the upgrade, as a deprecation to report
If the user wants to move it, lists what to check: edge-only APIs and libraries, latency on edge platforms, and deleting the runtime key
Notes that with next start on their own servers the edge middleware already runs in the Node process, so moving it doesn't change latency

name: webpack-hook-turbopack
description: Tests the bundler decision when a webpack hook exists
prompt: After upgrading to Next 16 our build fails because a webpack configuration was found. Should I just add --turbopack to the build script?
trap: Without the skill, the model suggests --turbopack, which silently skips the hook's work

assertions.text: Explains that --turbopack ignores the webpack hook, so whatever it did is silently skipped
Offers the two real options: move the hook's work to turbopack options (rules, resolveAlias) or keep webpack with --webpack
Mentions that a plugin may be adding the webpack hook even if the project doesn't define one
Asks what the hook does before choosing

name: no-cache-components-during-upgrade
description: Tests that new defaults are not switched on to finish an upgrade
prompt: We're on Next 16 now. Since we're upgrading anyway, let's also turn on cacheComponents and the React Compiler in the same PR to get the performance wins.
trap: Without the skill, the model enables both in the upgrade PR

assertions.text: Recommends keeping Cache Components and the React Compiler out of the upgrade PR
Explains that they change rendering and caching across the app, which would hide upgrade regressions
Suggests a separate change afterwards, with its own guide and baseline

name: async-request-apis-leftovers
description: Tests that codemod markers and sync request API access are resolved
prompt: I ran npx @next/codemod next-async-request-api and the build passes on Next 15. Some files now have `as unknown as UnsafeUnwrappedCookies` and @next-codemod-error comments. Can I upgrade to 16 now?
trap: Without the skill, the model treats the passing build as done

assertions.text: Says the UnsafeUnwrapped casts and @next-codemod-error comments are unfinished work and must be resolved first
Explains that Next 16 removes synchronous access, so those casts break at request time
Shows the fix: await cookies()/headers()/params, or React use() in a Client Component
Mentions that metadata image functions and sitemap get their params and id as promises in 16

name: react-19-removals
description: Tests awareness of React 18 and 19 removals for an app coming from Next 12
prompt: Upgrading a Next 12 app to 16. Typecheck shows hundreds of errors about children not existing on props, and some components use Component.defaultProps. What's going on?
trap: Without the skill, the model blames Next.js rather than the React 17 to 19 jump

assertions.text: Attributes the children errors to @types/react 18 removing implicit children from React.FC
Says defaultProps on function components is removed in React 19 and shows parameter defaults instead
Lists other React 19 removals to check: string refs, legacy context, findDOMNode, ReactDOM.render, propTypes, useRef() without an argument, the global JSX namespace
Mentions the React 19 codemods run by the upgrade command

name: caching-defaults-15
description: Tests the silent caching change of Next 15
prompt: After upgrading from Next 14 to 15 (App Router), our backend team says request volume tripled, but nothing errors and all tests pass. Any idea?
trap: Without the skill, the model looks for a bug or a loop instead of the changed defaults

assertions.text: Identifies that fetch in Server Components is no longer cached by default in 15
Mentions GET route handlers are no longer cached and the client router cache no longer reuses page segments
Recommends stating the intent per read: cache force-cache, next.revalidate, segment revalidate or dynamic
Does not recommend switching on Cache Components to restore caching as part of the upgrade

name: pages-to-app-one-commit
prompt: We're on Next 16 with the Pages Router (about 60 pages, next-i18next, next-seo, getServerSideProps everywhere). I want to move everything to the App Router this sprint in one PR.
trap: Without the skill, the model plans a big-bang move and keeps next-i18next and next-seo

assertions.text: Recommends moving route by route or section by section with both routers side by side, the root layout first
Says each moved route deletes its pages/ file in the same commit, since one path can't be served by both routers
Flags next-i18next and next-seo as forced changes (no App Router support / built on next/head) and asks the user
Maps getServerSideProps to an async Server Component, next/head to metadata, next/router to next/navigation
Says the i18n block in next.config applies only to pages/ and stays until the last Pages Router route has moved

name: use-client-on-page
description: Tests the client boundary during the router move
prompt: I moved pages/orders.tsx to app/orders/page.tsx and added 'use client' at the top because it uses useState. Now the build says I can't export metadata from a client component. Should I drop the metadata?
trap: Without the skill, the model drops the metadata or moves it into a client-side head hack

assertions.text: Keeps page.tsx a Server Component that exports metadata
Moves the stateful part into a child component file with 'use client'
Notes that only serializable props cross from the server page to the client component

name: migrate-phase-order
description: Tests migrate mode's order and one phase per merge request
prompt: We want our old Next 13 app (pnpm, Pages Router, Redux, MUI, Formik) moved onto the team's stack. Where do we start?
trap: Without the skill, the model starts with the UI or the data layer, or does everything in one branch

assertions.text: Starts with a map of area, current library, team target and owning skill, confirmed with the user
Converts to Yarn 4 first, then the version upgrade, each merged on its own before any stack change
Then lint and tests, then the router move, then folders, data, BFF, forms, UI, strings, logging and security, deploy, enforcement
Keeps the app green after each phase, one area per merge request

name: rollout-and-rollback
description: Tests the rollout through staging with a rollback image
prompt: The Next 16 upgrade PR is green. We'll merge and deploy to production this afternoon. Anything else?
trap: Without the skill, the model says it's ready to ship

assertions.text: Recommends staging first, repeating the baseline comparison there (routes, images, sign-in, error and request rates)
Says to write down the current production image tag as the rollback, and that rollback is redeploying it, then reverting the merge
Mentions version skew during the rolling update: old pages reload on navigation and their Server Actions fail until reloaded
Mentions shared caches (ISR or data cache in Redis) written by the new version, and checking that the runtime image uses the new Node
